story_text.value:
Hey HN!

I shared Optio here back in March. Originally it was focused on getting swarms of coding agents (claude code/codex) to drive PRs towards a merge by automatically resuming them on CI failures or PR comments.

Since then, I've reworked the project to be a general platform for running any kind of AI workflow on your infra by allowing users to configure each component of a possible workflow:

When: On demand, a cron schedule, or triggered by external events such as a webhook, slack message, ticket (jira/linear/gh), pagerduty/datadog/alertsmanager/pylon/sentry.

Where: In a k8s pod or any machine you have installed the optio daemon on (I use my laptop).

Who: Any harness you prefer (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Pi, etc.)

What/Why: You can format parameters from the triggers directly into the prompts and then configure if the agent should exit, be resumed automatically, or be persistent.

You can either define workflows in the web ui or as yaml files that get synced to the orchestrator (ai config-as-code).

I've also built native iOS and Android apps so you can connect to your cluster and create/manage agents remotely.

The marketing page is at https://optio.host and the code is still open source at https://github.com/jonwiggins/optio

Would love feedback or any thoughts you might have on how I could make it better!

title.value: Show HN: Optio – A self-hosted orchestration platform for AI agents

story_text.value:
Hey HN! As an avid user of cmux (https://cmux.com/), I wanted a way to control terminal and agent sessions from my Android phone, so I built Muxer. The app talks to a tiny relay over HTTPS, that then talks to cmux through its local socket, and gives you to ability to:

  - Answer agent permission requests, questions and plans from a notification
  - Reply to Claude Code, Codex and Pi chat sessions with text, voice, @ file mentions and photos
  - Receive all cmux notification, with inline replies, bubbles and background delivery.
  - Use a live terminal with sticky modifier keys and local scrollback
  - Share text and links from any app to an agent
  - Organize workspaces
  - Manage cmux Cloud VMs and automations
  - Lock the app with your fingerprint, face or screen lock
Enjoy, and let me know what you think!

story_text.value:
This is my own very opinionated take on personal accounting / budgeting for freelancers and small business owners operating in multiple currencies.

A lot of this is influenced by my circumstances:

- consultant / freelancer / business owner with multiple revenue streams - revenue fluctuates a lot and changes month to month - we're nomad, so currencies and shops change a lot, but categories stay stable - mobile and agentic first (PWA and MCP) with good desktop support on top - import from Wise, Plaid (so most banks), CSV, + screenshots and PDFs from mobile apps when all else fails - automatic categorization that does the right thing 90% of the time and learns for your corrections - deployed on a CloudFlare account (free account is usually enough)

Think of this as a template - just hand the repo URL to your agent and go wild. This is built to be infinitely malleable and extendable because accounting setups and needs differ so much between people.

Extracted from my own heavily used setup after removing all the private and unique bits.

May we all take control of our funds, each in our unique way.

story_text.value:
Hi HN, I'm Samar, a software engineer.

I built Junior because I was spending more time fixing CI issues, babysitting PRs and resolving merge conflicts.

I thought maybe i should automate all of it, and that's why I started building Junior. Junior is an agent that runs locally on macOS and picks up that kind of work. It connects with my Linear, Slack, Github etc and autopicks work for himself. It works on it and shares a report for me to review.

It's open source under. I'd love feedback, especially on the permission model and how autonomous should it work. Happy to answer anything.

story_text.value:
I have built an indie hacker project; my main flow was:

1. chatting with Claud Code about the general plan

2. assigning slices of work to other worker agents like Pi + DeepSeek 4.1 Flash

3. building in parallel

4. Claud Code reviews when done, runs tests, and merges after I validate

It worked, but with a lot of glue in the middle, so I built radian + arc into the same binary.

Radian: a compact, pragmatic agent that has enough tooling to solve a small coding task end to end; it does not try to be a plugin platform. You can still extend it via MCP, skills, or hooks to extend its capabilities. I think plugins are great, but a lot of them are for humans. I'm trying to remove humans from the loop. Humans are at the start and end of the loop.

arc: built into the radian binary;

* it can get work sent from another agent

* assign work items to concurrent headless radian agents

* automatically review, CICD, integrate locally

* humans can still be in the loop but not at the agent conversation or code review level, but at the work item approval/review level.

* shows all of the above in a plan view or Kanban board in TUI.

I have been heavily dogfooding, and Radian + arc basically built themselves in the last couple of weeks, with me just being a product manager/scrum master and qa.

radian + arc are open source at https://github.com/hisea/radian

What do you think about this approach? Looking for ideas to make Radian better or fit more scenarios.

title.value: Show HN: Radian, an agent puts development workflow on autopilot

story_text.value:
Hello everyone,

I am Elie a CS student in Switzerland, and for the past 3 months I've been building Swingback, a user feedback platform, with voting, Github/Linear integrations, and much more.

I started building this app as I was working on another project of mine and got really frustrated about the price and lack of features of the other platform (pay-per-user, no integration with Github, no translation, ...). So I've decided to go on (a much longer that I care to admit) sidequest building what is, for me, the perfect feedback platform.

Swingback has a free plan that you can use and will not stop people giving feedback (some of my competitors, for example, do not allow auto-signin (user being directly sing-in when opening the feedback tab), which add friction to people who wants to give feedback). There is also a paid plan, which include more integrations, removing the branding and other goodies.

It would mean the world if you guys would give Swingback a try. You can also check the Swingback feedback portal (https://feedback.swingback.dev) to see what feature are coming ;)

Best, Elie (aka Fayorg) https://eliebaier.ch

title.value: Show HN: Swingback, get feedback from your user for free

story_text.value:
I was playing around with visualising the S&P 500 by market cap and decided to add employees to each company's bubble.

What surprised me was how empty some of the biggest companies looked.

Nvidia is worth $5.2 trillion but employs only 42,000 people. That's around $124 million in market cap per employee. Meanwhile, Accenture employs 814,000 people and is worth $146 billion.

Each stick figure represents 10,000 employees. You can zoom in and explore individual companies.

I wrote a bit more about what I found here: https://bigwhalehunting.com/blog/workforce/

Would be interested to hear what you think.
